newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled lower for the first time since August 28, undermined by weakness in other bond markets, while a slightly weaker franc pared the recent strong gains in PIBOR contracts.
There was little reaction to the unveiling of the French budget today even though the central budget deficit came in higher than most had predicted at 283.7 billion francs.

Economists said although the deficit was slightly disappointing the fact that the government appeared committed to hitting the three percent Maastricht deficit target in 1997 left little reason for selling France against Germany.

"The markets have taken this Budget with a lot of calm and relaxation because there is much less doubt about the commitment of the government to pursue the goal of monetary union in 1999," said Jean Francois Mercier, economist at Salomon Brothers.
"As long as the markets perceive the road to EMU remains intact, there's little reason for an attack on the franc or bonds," he said.

The December bond future climbed gradually during the day with Bunds to reach a high 124.06, Tuesday's settlement price. Then the contract drifted lower with Bunds to settle at 123.86, down 20 centimes on the day.
Traders were not too concerned about today's decline as they said the bond market needed to take a breather after the impressive gains so far this month.
They said the contract would now probably remain range bound until the Fed's policy meeting on September 24 to see whether interest rates will be raised or not.
Traders also said the market would probably be supported by domestic investors with cash to invest although they might wait for some further declines before putting their money into bonds.
The 10-year spread over Bunds widened slightly on Wednesday to five basis points from three yesterday.
Most economists were still expecting the Bank of France to cut interest rates on Thursday, although some had revised their expectations down to just a small easing in call money.
Philippe Brossard, economist at ABN Amro in Paris, said "Obviously if the Bank of France does not cut rates it's going to create tension with the government again."
Asked in an interview with Reuters financial television on Wednesday whether the budget paved the way for lower interest rates, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said "yes, certainly."
The Bank of France monetary policy council meets on Thursday. Any rate change would be announced from 1115 GMT.
December PIBOR settled down five at 96.17, underperforming the equivalent Euromark contract.
Traders said the franc come under pressure early on Wednesday from profit taking and some options-related trades though volume was relatively light.
The currency was trading at 3.4065 per mark at 1625 GMT, off the day's low at 3.4092 but well below Tuesday's opening level of 3.3975.
